title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: Ps 32:1–2 — no lynx-eye sees immediate Adam-imputation there
pass_a_gloss: Second you dig out of Ps. 32:1–2 the blessedness of forgiven, covered, uncharged sin—by a craft Placeus may wonder at more than catch. Even a lynx-keen mind's eye cannot spot there an immediate charging of Adam's actual deed to all offspring. You pile words to make him see it with you; he cannot. Better you had restated the force in plain syllogism than drowned it in a heap of words he cannot mine.
pass_b_english: Your second Argument you carve out from Ps. 32:1–2. Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered: Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed iniquity—by an art which I may admire more than follow. For what eye of the mind, however lynx-keen, could see in those words the immediate imputation of Adam's actual sin to the whole posterity? You nevertheless try with many words to make me see it with you in them, but I cannot. Would that you had rewoven the force of your argument in applied syllogistic form, and not buried it under a great abundance of words; from which I cannot dig it out.
source_text: Secundum tuum Argumentum exsculpis ex Ps. 32. 1. 2. Beatus cui dimittitur praevaricatio, cui tegitur peccatum: Beatus homo cui non imputavit Dominus iniquitatem, ea arte, quam mihi mirari magis licet, quam assequi. Quis enim mentis oculus, ut ut lynceus, videre possit in illis verbis immediatam peccati actualis Adami toti posteritati imputationem? Tu tamen multis verbis efficere conaris, ut eam tecum in illis videam, sed non possum. Utinam tui argumenti vim adhibita forma syllogistica retexuisses, nec magna verborum copia obruisses; ex quibus eam eruere non possum.
